doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: His son's trumpet career and songwriting together
summary: His son Michael, a trumpeter, won a Grammy-sponsored award and toured with Steely Dan alongside his daughter; father and son discuss songwriting.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: He plays trumpet. You know he graduated from school in music and art in 1992, won a Grammy as the outstanding musician in the country, the Grammy people, NARAS, the Grammy people did a contest, and he won this big award. He was also a presidential scholar in some other area for being in the arts. So bingo, he was a sudden person of the week on ABC news, this 18-year-old kid.
You know now that you mention it, I know I’ve seen his name in the trades or whatever, and I didn’t make the connection. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

Right. And he went around the world with this U.S. super band and he was getting more publicity than you can imagine. All of a sudden he’s a songwriter, a singer, a pianist, a guitar player, a drummer, and all kinds of things. And a beautiful trumpet player. But he’s just like spread out to here right now. So he’s finding his way with music, extremely expressive, sometimes out, sometimes in, but it’s gorgeous stuff, I mean I find it gorgeous stuff. So he’s going to find his way in the world, and my daughter is a singer and they were both out with Steely Dan for instance, two years, they’ve both been on a world tour with Steely Dan. And they’re good. I mean, trust a prejudiced father. And they’re just trying to find their way. I don’t know where we’re going with this conversation.
Well do you compare songwriting with — do you compare your songs with your son? Do you guys get together?

Oh all the time, all the time. We talk. We don’t try to write songs like each other, but I listen to his stuff and it leaks through. He’s being as original as he can be, but I hear myself all the time in there in a certain way. But he’s very original. Actually we don’t talk technique of songwriting at all. We talk about the soul of the songwriting, writing about what’s on your mind, and enjoying it. It’s like a professional hobby with both of us. We’re both very dedicated to it. And he’s done, well I’ve done, I mean I just don’t write pop songs, I just write stuff that’s really on my mind, whether it’s serious or joking, and sometimes joking is very serious to me. I mean it just is, that’s just how I express myself.
